full_text_en:
Ji Xuanzhi v. Ji Yaqin — inheritance dispute over house

Plaintiff: Ji Xuanzhi, female, 64 years old, residing at No. 153, Kaiyuan Road, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Xue Laiwang, 47 years old, son of the plaintiff, worker.

Agent ad litem: Li Peifeng, lawyer from Xiamen First Law Firm.

Defendant: Ji Yaqin, female, 57 years old, residing at No. 26, Xiahe Xiang, Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

Agent ad litem: Bai Zhongfu, 34 years old, son of the defendant.

Agent ad litem: Yin Shenping, lawyer from Xiamen First Law Firm.

The plaintiff, Ji Xuanzhi, brought a lawsuit against the defendant, Ji Yaqin, over a dispute concerning inheritance of a house, and filed the complaint with the Kaiyuan District People's Court of Xiamen City, Fujian Province.

During the litigation, the defendant, Ji Yaqin, without authorization, removed the fourth floor of the disputed building, intending to renovate it. To facilitate the trial of the case and the enforcement of the judgment, the Kaiyuan District People's Court, on July 8, 1987, pursuant to Article 92(1) and Article 93(2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China (for Trial Implementation), issued a property preservation ruling ex officio, sealing up the fourth floor of the building at No. 26, Xiahe Xiang.

The Kaiyuan District People's Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and conducted a public trial of the case, and found the following:

The plaintiff and the defendant are biological sisters. The four-story building located at No. 26, Xiahe Xiang, Xiamen City, was jointly built by the parties' biological father, Ji Jingshan, and biological mother, Chen Shu, and the property title was registered in the name of Chen Shu. The decedents had two sons and two daughters: the eldest son, Ji Tianhe, and the second son, Ji Naishun, went to Taiwan Province to seek a livelihood before liberation, and their whereabouts have been unknown ever since. The eldest daughter, Ji Xuanzhi, was adopted by others from childhood; the second daughter, Ji Yaqin, lived with her mother, Chen Shu, for a long time. The first, third, and fourth floors of the disputed building were nationalized, while the second floor was occupied by Chen Shu and the defendant. Later, the third and fourth floors of the building, which had been nationalized, were returned under the policy, and Chen Shu rented them out. Although the plaintiff was adopted by others from childhood, she maintained contact with her biological mother after reaching adulthood and provided care in many aspects of life. When Chen Shu was ill in her later years, the plaintiff attended to her. In January 1986, Chen Shu passed away, and the plaintiff and the defendant jointly arranged the funeral. Thereafter, the plaintiff proposed to inherit and divide the building that was Chen Shu's estate, but the defendant disagreed, leading to a dispute. Through mediation by relatives and the neighborhood committee, the defendant agreed to pay RMB 6,000 as compensation to the plaintiff. Later, the defendant reneged, and the plaintiff filed the lawsuit with the Kaiyuan District People's Court. The plaintiff alleged: The plaintiff is one of the statutory heirs and fulfilled the duty of support for the biological mother during her lifetime, and thus claimed the right to inherit the mother's estate; the brothers Ji Tianhe and Ji Naishun have had no news since going to Taiwan, and out of sibling affection, the plaintiff agreed to reserve their shares of inheritance, to be managed by the plaintiff and the defendant respectively on their behalf.

The defendant defended: The plaintiff was adopted by others when she was two months old, and the rights and obligations between her and her biological mother were thereby extinguished; therefore, she cannot serve as a statutory heir of the biological mother. However, out of sisterly affection and given that she visited the biological mother during holidays, the defendant was willing to handle the plaintiff's claim through financial compensation (a compensation of RMB 6,000, to be paid in installments over six years, at RMB 1,000 per year), but the plaintiff must deliver the title deed of the building to the defendant for safekeeping.

The Kaiyuan District People's Court held at trial: The second, third, and fourth floors of the building at No. 26, Xiahe Xiang are the estate of the decedents Ji Jingshan and Chen Shu. Pursuant to Article 10(2) of the Inheritance Law of the People's Republic of China, they shall be jointly inherited by the statutory first-order heirs Ji Yaqin, Ji Tianhe, and Ji Naishun; since Ji Tianhe and Ji Naishun went to Taiwan and their whereabouts are unknown, their inheritance shares shall be reserved. Ji Xuanzhi was given for adoption to others from childhood and has maintained an adoptive relationship with her adoptive parents. Pursuant to Article 20(2) of the Marriage Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "the rights and obligations between adopted children and their biological parents are extinguished upon the establishment of the adoptive relationship," the plaintiff cannot serve as a statutory heir of the decedents and therefore cannot inherit the estate of Chen Shu. However, in view of the fact that the plaintiff provided long-term care and financial support to Chen Shu during her lifetime, in accordance with Article 14 of the Inheritance Law, which provides that "persons other than the heirs who have provided more support to the decedent may be given an appropriate share of the estate," the plaintiff may be given an appropriate share of Chen Shu's estate. The defendant's proposal to offer RMB 6,000 as compensation for the plaintiff's share of the decedent's estate is acceptable and shall be supported; as for the payment period, it may be shortened as appropriate. The defendant's request that the plaintiff return the title deed of the building to facilitate the defendant's renovation of the building is reasonable.

In conclusion, on August 31, 1987, the court rendered the following judgment:

1. The second, third, and fourth floors of the building at No. 26, Xiahe Xiang shall be jointly inherited by the defendant Ji Yaqin and Ji Tianhe and Ji Naishun, who are in Taiwan;

2. The defendant Ji Yaqin shall compensate the plaintiff Ji Xuanzhi in the amount of RMB 6,000, with RMB 2,000 to be paid upon the effectiveness of this judgment, RMB 2,000 to be paid six months after effectiveness, and RMB 2,000 to be paid one year after effectiveness; the plaintiff shall deliver the title deed of the disputed building to the defendant after the defendant has paid the above amount in full.

Court costs for this case: RMB 395, with RMB 95 to be borne by the plaintiff and RMB 300 by the defendant.

After the judgment was pronounced, the plaintiff, Ji Xuanzhi, refused to accept it, claiming that the decedent Chen Shu did not give her up for adoption and that she had fulfilled substantial obligations, and therefore requested to inherit Chen Shu's estate according to law. She appealed to the Xiamen Intermediate People's Court.

The Xiamen Intermediate People's Court held at trial: The appellant, Ji Xuanzhi, was adopted by others from childhood, and her rights and obligations with her biological mother were extinguished by law; thus, she cannot inherit the decedent's estate as a statutory heir. However, the appellant provided considerable support to the decedent during her lifetime; after the decedent's death, the appellant and the appellee jointly arranged the funeral. Therefore, the appellant may be given an appropriate share of Chen Shu's estate according to law. Considering the appellant's degree of support to the decedent during her lifetime, the amount apportioned to the appellant was relatively low and may be appropriately increased. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 151(1) of the Civil Procedure Law (for Trial Implementation), on June 1, 1988, the court rendered the following judgment:

The first item of the original judgment is affirmed; the second item is modified as follows: Ji Yaqin, Ji Tianhe, and Ji Naishun shall jointly compensate Ji Xuanzhi in the amount of RMB 8,000, being the portion of the property value apportionable to her, and before Ji Tianhe and Ji Naishun actually take possession of the property, this amount shall first be paid by Ji Yaqin. Ji Yaqin shall pay RMB 4,000 within six months after this judgment becomes effective, and the balance shall be paid in full within one year. Ji Xuanzhi shall, after Ji Yaqin has paid the above amount in full, deliver the title deed of the disputed building to Ji Yaqin for safekeeping.

Court costs for the second instance: RMB 395, with RMB 200 to be borne by Ji Xuanzhi and RMB 195 by Ji Yaqin.
